title: Weight‑Only 8‑bit (WO8) GPTQ/AWQ integration pipeline and numerical regression harness
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Build a deterministic integration and regression test pipeline for weight‑only 8‑bit (WO8) profiles produced by GPTQ/AWQ toolchains. The goal is to validate numeric fidelity and downstream quality for a representative set of models, automate nightly calibration runs, and gate releases with statistical acceptance criteria.

Background: We already ingest GPTQ/AWQ artifacts from the model onboarding flow, but coverage is ad hoc: per‑run reports live in various buckets and manual signoff is required for releases. This ticket consolidates: a) canonical calibration harness that replays calibration snapshots, b) a reproducible numerical comparison runner (golden seeds + deterministic RNG), and c) CI/regtest integration that blocks model profile promotion on measurable regressions.

Goals:
- Establish a single WO8 verification pipeline that accepts GPTQ and AWQ artifacts and outputs a standardized JSON report.
- Define statistical tests (paired metric deltas, non‑inferiority margins) for LM quality across generation, embedding similarity, and perplexity.
- Automate daily calibration runs and a canary rollout path that exercises live inference on dedicated dev capacity.
- Add drift detection alerts when nightly runs exceed thresholds.

Constraints & assumptions:
- We must support models with KV cache and long context (>8k) without changing runtime kernels.
- Reproducibility required: use deterministic seeds and record exact kernel/quant config.
- Performance regressions up to 3% token latency allowed during canary; anything beyond triggers automatic fallback to FP16 variant.

Success criteria:
- CI job "wo8-quant-verifier" runs on every profile PR and returns PASS/FAIL with human‑readable diagnostics.
- Nightly job produces time‑series of the defined metrics and creates an alert if any model exceeds the delta threshold.
- Release tooling refuses promotion of a quant profile if tests fail and lists the failing assertion in the release notes.
acceptance_criteria: CI job returns JSON report with fields: model, profile-id, seed, kernel-version, metrics
Non‑inferiority test passes for 90% of benchmark prompts with margin <= 1.5% on top‑1 token accuracy
Perplexity delta against FP16 baseline < 2.0% for conversational test set
Nightly job creates baseline snapshot and retention for 30 days
Canary route executes 10k tokens of production‑like traffic with telemetry and auto‑rollback on failure
approach: Stage 1: Ingest GPTQ/AWQ artifacts into a canonical S3 layout with manifest metadata (sha256, build tag, quant params)
Stage 2: Run deterministic calibration replay harness using golden calibration datasets (translation, long‑context, instruction) and capture logits + embeddings
Stage 3: Compute numeric comparisons: bit‑level checks where applicable, per‑token logit delta histograms, and embedding cosine distributions
Stage 4: Wrap comparisons into statistical tests (paired t, Wilcoxon where non‑normal) and produce PASS/FAIL with p‑values and effect sizes
Stage 5: Integrate with CI (GitHub Actions) to gate model profile merges and with Console telemetry for nightly dashboards
test_plan: Unit tests for deterministic runner (seed control, RNG drift checks)
Synthetic regression suite: 50 prompts across genres, golden responses stored in artifacts repo
Scale test: run entire harness against three representative models (Llama‑like 13B, MPT‑30B, Open architecture 70B) in dedicated dev cluster
Chaos test: inject quantization noise via modified scale factors and assert detection by regression runner
End‑to‑end: profile PR -> CI run -> nightly baseline -> canary traffic -> rollback scenario

Use staggered canary with automatic rollback to FP16 when latency or quality regressions exceed thresholds
Limit nightly full‑log storage to 7 days for all runs, retain only failing runs for 90 days to reduce cost
